slices.name: ws01-31-heritage-layout
slices.brief:
WS01 slice 31 of 32 (checkpoint D, the design system; slices 20 to 32; its draft PR is #108). Branch redesign/ws01-design-system, HEAD 0cc7c30 (slice 30's own commit); the base for diffs is 0cc7c30. Checkpoints A, B and C are merged to main and live. The harness commit before slice 30 (abe7d07) gave each browser-test server its own database in test/a11y/global-setup.ts and made the baseline sampler, the hero-ring test and the scroll panel's arrow-key test wait or press until done; slice 30 changed no file under test/a11y, so nothing there has moved since. Every line number below was measured on the working tree that held slice 30 finished and not yet committed, the tree this slice starts from; slice 30's commit is expected to hold exactly those files, but read any file before you edit it and do not trust a cited line without looking at it. Read first: REDESIGN_STATUS.md (Ordering rules, lines 7 to 11; the acceptance table with its AC11 row (line 35), AC12 row (line 36) and AC13 row (line 37), all still Planned and all owned by step 31, so this slice fills all three, with the AC10 row (line 34), AC4 row (line 28) and AC7 row (line 31) as the pattern for a filled row and the AC8 row (line 32) left alone; the step 30 block (lines 837 to 874) in full, above all its Files (line 841), The fallback faces (848), The tokens (849), The hooks (850), The guard and the layer (853), ThemeScope (854), The places left for later (858), Judgement calls (859 to 870), Build (872) and Checks (874), with the step 29 block (lines 804 to 835) and step 28 block (lines 772 to 802) as the pattern for a step block and the step 22 block (lines 560 to 573: ThemeScope 568, Nesting 569, routeScope 570, Fonts 571, the fixture page 572) for what the scope already does; Decisions (heading at line 876): The scope switches need newLook (step 21), line 932; One scope mechanism (step 22), line 935; the five step 30 lines, 965 to 969, which this slice leaves word for word; Deviations (heading at line 971): the one planned line for this step, 'AC13 compares screenshots from the same run (step 31)', line 1091, which this slice keeps word for word and marks done, with 'Small caps (step 30)', line 1090, as the pattern for a planned line marked done; the Step 30 entry, lines 1263 to 1273, as the pattern for a deviation entry, with its sub-bullet 'Files beyond the step's list:' (line 1273) and the sub-bullet at line 1272 on the stylesheet arriving after the scope's first paint; Verify items (heading at line 1275): the step 30 ones, lines 1508 to 1529, as the pattern, above all 'The hooks (step 30)' (1514), 'The 32 px floor (step 30)' (1515), 'Heritage waits for newLook (step 30)' (1516), 'Georgia is not installed (step 30)' (1517), 'The tests that move (step 30)' (1521) and 'The retry after a failed load (step 30)' (1529); Follow-ups (heading at line 1531): the step 30 ones, lines 1701 to 1707, above all 'The heritage stylesheet before the first paint (step 30)' (1707), which this slice answers, 'Hooks for the heritage pages (step 30)' (1703), 'The fallback faces measured (step 30)' (1702) and 'Georgia on the test computers (step 30)' (1704); and, older, 'ThemeScope as a page's main (step 22)' (1631), 'Base inside heritage in a browser (step 22)' (1632), 'AC11 and AC12 second halves (step 22)' (1634), 'Classes only docs and tests name reach the CSS (step 23)' (1638), 'Heritage on a muted panel (step 24)' (1654), 'The About logo in the heritage layout (step 28)' (1689), 'The seal from the rook (step 28)' (1690), 'Pages wider than a phone, and a main inside a main (step 28; older than the step)' (1693) and 'K reviews the step 30 judgement calls (step 30)' (1701) as the pattern for a K-reviews follow-up), docs/redesign/REDESIGN_SPEC.md (the heritage row of the looks table, line 137, whose words put data-theme on main; the files list, line 342, which names HeritageLayout, ThickThinRule and Seal; acceptance criteria 11, 12 and 13, lines 358 to 360; the test list, lines 366 to 369; the WS01 deviations list, line 112, which ends with the step 30 sentence), docs/redesign/DESIGN_REPLAN_phase0.md (lines 80 to 109: the two levels, what heritage changes and never changes, lines 102 and 103, small caps and Caslon at 106, the dark rule at 108; line 128, the new primitives; line 156, what WS01 grows by, which lists an accessibility pass on three heritage pages and a layout shift check; line 600, the layout's file list; line 888, item 13), docs/redesign/decided-boards/Looks-Applied.dc.html (Level A, the six routes, one thick-thin rule per section, the seal, the 2px radius, controls never change) and docs/redesign/lca-redesign-boards/boards/Looks-1-Heritage-Page.dc.html (the rule drawn as a 6px high box, 3px solid on top and 1px solid below, navy, or gold on navy), src/App.tsx (all 145 lines: the lazy page imports, lines 14 to 46; the site's main, line 61; the Suspense and its loading line, lines 62 to 73; the six routes, lines 100, 101, 105, 106, 108 and 111; the fixture route, lines 135 to 137), src/lib/themeScopes.ts (HERITAGE_ROUTES, line 43; routeScope, line 86; nestingProblem, line 99), src/components/ThemeScope.tsx (the header comment, lines 1 to 30; SCOPE_FONTS, lines 43 to 46; loadScopeFonts, lines 50 to 63; the effect that calls it, lines 81 to 83), src/styles/themes/heritage.css (209 lines: the hooks and rules, lines 157 to 209), src/lib/features.ts (newLook, line 44; themeHeritage, line 50; FEATURES, line 194), src/areas/governance/components/GovLayout.tsx (the inner main, line 87), src/areas/governance/components/GovernanceDocuments.tsx (the lazy editor, lines 27 to 45; the add and edit card, lines 269 to 338, with its two editor calls at lines 285 and 324), src/components/PageHero.tsx (its h1 at lines 95 and 99), src/components/LcaMark.tsx, src/pages/AboutPage.tsx (the logo frame, lines 16 to 21), the other five heritage pages (BoardPage, BylawsPage, MinutesPage, AnnualMeetingPage, ChampionsPage), src/pages/fixtures/ScopeFixturePage.tsx (352 lines; its one ThemeScope, line 84), src/index.css (the base look's tokens, lines 395 to 415 and 457 to 472; the heritage colours, lines 603 to 630; the shadcn variables repeated on every scope, lines 693 to 722; the focus ring, line 730), src/components/ui/button.tsx and src/components/ui/input.tsx, and the tests that pin what this slice touches: test/unit/themeScopes.test.ts (lines 134 to 206) and themeScopes-edges.test.ts (lines 52 to 72), test/unit/contrast.test.ts (lines 361 to 419) and goldText.test.ts (lines 713 to 724), test/unit/app-routes.test.tsx (all of it), test/unit/theme-scope-wiring.test.ts (all of it), theme-scope.test.tsx and theme-scope-edges.test.tsx, test/unit/heritage-edges.test.ts (lines 369 to 505), heritage-css.test.ts and heritage-scope-edges.test.tsx, test/unit/lca-mark.test.tsx (lines 124 to 136), test/unit/brand-placements.test.tsx (the mock of FEATURES, lines 41 to 57), test/unit/tokens-scopes.test.ts (lines 25 to 40), test/unit/redesign-status-step30.test.ts (all of it, so the step 31 records leave its expectations true once its three acceptance row pins are brought up), test/unit/browser-test-wiring.test.ts (lines 455 to 480), test/a11y/support.ts, test/a11y/scope-switch.spec.ts (lines 100 to 227), test/a11y/brand.spec.ts (lines 243 to 300) and brand-edges.spec.ts (lines 269 to 312), test/a11y/global-setup.ts (lines 70 to 75, the two builds' switches), and test/a11y/baseline.ts and baseline.json, so that the flag-off baseline comparison stays green. The lead's notes win over this brief and the manifest where they differ (they say nothing on this slice beyond the standing rules and the two notes on the harness, which every step must leave alone): <scratchpad>/ws01-lead-notes.md. The manifest entry (order 31) is in <scratchpad>/ws01-manifest.json. Environment facts for this container: the pinned Playwright expects a Chromium build the container does not have, so every npm run test:a11y here runs as PW_CHROMIUM_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium npm run test:a11y (the config reads that variable); never run playwright install; WRANGLER_SEND_METRICS=false on every wrangler command; localhost is exempt from the outbound proxy, so the a11y servers on 127.0.0.1 work. node_modules is installed, both heritage font packages included, and neither is changed by this slice; nothing ever runs against a remote database or the Cloudflare account; agents never commit, stash, reset or check out anything; the working tree is the only copy. Georgia is not installed in this container (fc-list finds no Georgia and no face made to match its metrics; the serif faces on this computer are DejaVu Serif, FreeSerif and Liberation Serif), so a browser test here draws the device's serif while a heritage face loads and never the fallback faces; see difference 6. This slice expects to add no dependency. If the layout shift check truly needs a face with Georgia's metrics, prefer a font file the test writes or one already on this computer; a package is allowed only as an exact-pinned development dependency (no caret) published on or before 2026-10-08 (today is 2026-10-22, so two weeks old), with package-lock.json updated by npm install through the proxy, and the record says so. If an install fails, say so with the error and stop that part: do not vendor files, loosen a pin or disable TLS checks. The branch tip is 0cc7c30 and the working tree is clean when the slice starts; origin/redesign/ws01-design-system carries later commits only once the lead pushes, and the local main ref does not carry the checkpoint merges, so a diff against the local main shows far more than this slice: take this slice's own changes as the working tree against 0cc7c30. A full test:a11y run starts servers on ports 8801 and 8802 (each over a database of its own; read test/a11y/global-setup.ts for where), so never run two of them at once, and never run one while a build is running. Build exactly this. Ship the Heritage Club scope on its six pages behind themeHeritage. src/layouts/HeritageLayout.tsx is a lazy layout route in App.tsx. It wraps AboutPage, BoardPage, BylawsPage, MinutesPage, AnnualMeetingPage and ChampionsPage in ThemeScope scope="heritage", keeping GovLayout inside, and is active only when FEATURES.themeHeritage is on. With the flag off, the route elements are exactly as today. AboutPage keeps slice 28's LcaLogo on its white or cream mat inside the scope. GovernanceDocuments (src/areas/governance/components) wraps its form and the lazy RichTextEditor in ThemeScope scope="base", the data-theme="" reset, only when themeHeritage is on, and the wrapper uses display: contents, so the flag-off DOM and layout are unchanged. New ornaments: ThickThinRule.tsx (a CSS thick-thin rule) and Seal.tsx (an SVG built from LcaMark, brand gold used only as a rule or seal). themeScopes.test.ts is extended to extract every route path from App.tsx and fail if any admin, workspace, manage, dashboard, account or board inbox route resolves to heritage. test/unit/governanceEditors.test.tsx renders RichTextEditor and the GovernanceDocuments form inside HeritageLayout and asserts that the closest [data-theme] above each is "", and that with themeHeritage off no ThemeScope wrapper is rendered. test/a11y/heritage.spec.ts has three parts: the heritage CSS chunk and font files never appear in the / network log; CLS on /about and /governance/bylaws stays under 0.1 across the font swap; and element screenshots of Button, Input, StatusBadge and a focused control, taken in the same run inside heritage and base, are pixel-identical.

Verify items from the manifest, each to be re-checked against the tree as it is now (the earlier finding follows): Pages and editors exist. (AboutPage, BoardPage, BylawsPage, MinutesPage, AnnualMeetingPage and ChampionsPage are lazy routes in App.tsx (/about, /governance/board, /governance/bylaws, /governance/minutes, /meeting, /champions). GovLayout, GovernanceDocuments and RichTextEditor moved to src/areas/governance/components in slice 19; GovernanceDocuments lazy-loads RichTextEditor and is used by MinutesPage. Re-checked: it holds in part. The six pages are lazy routes (imports at lines 14, 15, 19, 20, 21 and 33 of src/App.tsx; routes as in difference 1), and GovLayout, GovernanceDocuments, RichTextEditor and OfficerPhoto are in src/areas/governance/components. But GovLayout is drawn by four of the six, not six (difference 2); GovernanceDocuments is drawn by BylawsPage, three times, as well as by MinutesPage, twice (difference 8); and RichTextEditor is also imported, statically, by two admin screens that are always base, src/areas/admin/components/PostsPanel.tsx (line 12) and src/pages/AdminEmailPage.tsx (line 8).) Further differences between the manifest's assumptions and the tree, all measured at the tree this slice starts from (slice 30 finished). (1) The folder is new and the routes' shape is pinned. src/layouts does not exist (src holds App.tsx, areas, assets, components, contexts, hooks, lib, pages and styles). The six routes are one-line routes in the single Routes list of src/App.tsx, inside the site's main (line 61) and its Suspense (lines 62 to 73, whose loading line is a py-24 row): /meeting at line 100, /about 101, /governance/board 105, /champions 106, /governance/bylaws 108 and /governance/minutes 111, each written <Route path="..." element={<XPage />} />; the three redirects (/governance 104, /state-champions 107, /governance/rules 110) sit among them and stay as they are. The header and the footer are outside the Routes, so they are always base, as the spec requires. Pins on that shape that this slice keeps true or moves: test/unit/contrast.test.ts (lines 361 to 372) and test/unit/goldText.test.ts (lines 713 to 724) each find a heritage route's page by the pattern <Route path="<route>" element={<Page />} and throw when a route is written any other way, which includes wrapping its element; test/unit/themeScopes.test.ts (lines 134 to 206) and themeScopes-edges.test.ts (lines 52 to 72) read every <Route path="..."> and every Navigate redirect from App.tsx, require each of the six exactly once, and require exactly the six to resolve to heritage; test/unit/app-routes.test.tsx (lines 21 to 33) reads every lazy( call in App.tsx, requires 33 pages whose specifiers all match @/pages/<Name>, and loads each, so a lazy layout in src/layouts fails it on its count and on its pattern: move that pin and say how. One shape that keeps the first four: a pathless layout route, <Route element={<HeritageLayout />}>, holding the six routes written once and unchanged, chosen by the flag at the top of App.tsx (the six routes as one constant fragment, wrapped in the layout route or not according to FEATURES.themeHeritage), so with the flag off the route list is today's. src/App.tsx must not name ThemeScope (test/unit/theme-scope-wiring.test.ts, lines 31 to 35): it names the layout only. (2) GovLayout serves four of the six pages, not six. AboutPage (line 11), BoardPage (268), BylawsPage (15) and MinutesPage (14) draw GovLayout; AnnualMeetingPage (PageHero at line 107) and ChampionsPage (PageHero at line 53) draw PageHero directly, so those two have no GovLayout to keep inside. GovLayout draws PageHero, then a section with its sidebar and a main element at line 87, so on the four pages a main sits inside the site's main (the follow-up at line 1693 leaves the fix to WS14 or this slice; the accessibility checker's WCAG rules report neither, and test/a11y/brand-edges.spec.ts line 283 relies on there being two). The spec's table (docs/redesign/REDESIGN_SPEC.md line 137) says data-theme="heritage" goes on main, but ThemeScope's header (lines 4 to 14) and the follow-up at line 1631 say a scope must not be a page's main, since src/App.tsx already wraps every route in one and a second landmark would be reported. Use a div inside the site's main and record the difference from the spec's words. Changing GovLayout's inner main to a plain element changes the flag-off markup of four pages, so either leave it and say so, or change it only when the layout is active; record which. (3) A scope draws no ground by default. ThemeScope's default layout is display: contents, so heritage's tokens reach the page's children but nothing paints the paper ground (--ground, #f7f3e8 in the light look) unless the wrapper is layout="box" with a ground class, as the fixture page's is (src/pages/fixtures/ScopeFixturePage.tsx, line 84: layout="box" className="bg-background text-foreground"). The layout therefore uses layout="box" on a div with a ground and ink class (bg-ground reads the token itself; see difference 9 before choosing bg-background), inside the site's main, and the ground has to run down to the footer on a short page (Minutes with no documents, for one): check it at 1280 and 390 pixels, light and dark. The header and footer keep the base look: a test shows neither has a data-theme ancestor on a heritage page. (4) None of the six pages carries a heritage hook. src/styles/themes/heritage.css (lines 163 to 209) styles only elements that carry data-heritage words (display on an h1 or h2, figure, reader, card, table, mat), the small-caps class and the logo frame's slot; nothing is styled by its tag alone, so a heritage page looks like the base look on new grounds until its elements are hooked (the follow-up at line 1703 gives that to this slice). PageHero's h1 (src/components/PageHero.tsx, lines 95 and 99) is text-3xl sm:text-4xl with no hook, and PageHero is imported by 12 files; the pages' section headings are text-base, text-lg or text-xl (20 pixels at most), under the 32 pixel floor, so they take no display hook and keep the base face; the display hook goes on each page's h1 only. Display figures ('1915', '300+') are on none of the six pages (they are in HomePage.tsx, Footer.tsx and ClubsPage.tsx), so figure has no use here and no copy is added to give it one. The boxes that take the 2px radius are the cards the pages draw as rounded-xl border bg-card (for example BoardPage lines 63 and 336, AnnualMeetingPage lines 130 and 224, ChampionsPage lines 70, 95 and 131, the last the table's frame) and the About logo frame, which already carries its slot. The hooks must be on the elements only when the page is drawn in the layout: with the flag off the markup of the six pages stays today's to the attribute (test/unit/brand-placements.test.tsx and test/unit/fixtures/brand-today.ts hold /about's markup literally with the switches off). One way is a small context that the layout provides and PageHero, GovLayout and the pages read to add their hooks, which leaves PageHero's other users untouched even with the flag on; another is to set the attributes from FEATURES.themeHeritage in each file. Decide, and record it as a judgement call. The reader hook is WS14's and small caps WS10's; add neither. Files this adds to the step: src/components/PageHero.tsx, GovLayout.tsx and the six pages. (5) The look's stylesheet arrives after the scope's first paint unless this slice changes that. ThemeScope asks for src/styles/themes/heritage.css in an effect (src/components/ThemeScope.tsx, lines 81 to 83), so a hooked element is drawn in the base type and moves when the file arrives; step 30 measured that shift at 0.0145 for a heading and 0.0964 with a reading column added, before any face swapped (follow-up at line 1707; deviation at line 1272), against AC11's 0.1. That follow-up asks this slice to load the file before heritage content paints and to handle a failed load itself, since in a built site a second import() of a stylesheet that failed resolves at once and fetches nothing (verify item at line 1529). The manifest lists neither ThemeScope.tsx nor a loader. One way is the follow-up's: ThemeScope, or a module of its own that only ThemeScope names, keeps one promise of the import, which resolves when the stylesheet has loaded, and the layout's lazy route waits for it, adding a fresh link of its own after a failure (the file's ?url import gives the address, or a query sets it apart from the one that failed); a function exported beside a component draws the react-refresh/only-export-components lint warning, so the loader may need a file of its own. Pins that move with it: test/unit/theme-scope-wiring.test.ts (only ThemeScope imports heritage.css, lazily and beside live.css, lines 44 to 53), test/unit/theme-scope.test.tsx and theme-scope-edges.test.tsx (their mocks of the stylesheet), and test/unit/heritage-edges.test.ts (lines 369 to 398 build ThemeScope's import and expect one chunk to hold it). ThemeScope still names no switch (wiring test lines 55 to 59): the gate on themeHeritage lives in HeritageLayout and GovernanceDocuments. (6) AC11's 0.1 is not only the font swap, and a face with Georgia's metrics is not available here. Step 30 measured, in Chromium on both browser-test builds (follow-up at line 1707), the stylesheet arriving after the first paint (difference 5) and a shift that is not the look's at all: on a page the site loads on demand the footer moves when the page takes the place of the Suspense loading line, 0.67 to 0.69 on /about and /governance/bylaws at 390 by 844 pixels and 0.22 to 0.35 at 1280 by 800, with newLook off as well, against 0.0057 to 0.0066 on /. A check of /about and /governance/bylaws that adds every layout-shift entry from the start of the navigation cannot come in under 0.1 unless that shift is dealt with. Say which you do and why: hold the page's height while it loads, only inside the layout and with the flag on (the layout's own Suspense with a fallback that reserves the height), since changing the loading line in src/App.tsx changes every lazy page with the switches off; or measure the font swap apart from the page's arrival (for example counting entries only after the page's heading is drawn and its data has arrived) and say that is what was measured. The layout also adds a wait: its own chunk arrives before the page's, two lazy steps in a row instead of one. /governance/bylaws draws a plain Loading line in each of its three GovernanceDocuments before the list (GovernanceDocuments.tsx, line 256), a shift that belongs to the data, so the check waits for the lists. Step 30's records ask for two measurements of the swap, one with a face that has Georgia's metrics and one with no Georgia, as phones that have none draw it (follow-ups at lines 1702 and 1704). Here only the second kind can be made unless you supply a face with those metrics for the test (see the environment facts) and say which. Do not claim a figure for a run that was not made; if only the no-Georgia run is made, say so and leave the other to K as a follow-up. If the swap with no Georgia is over 0.1, the follow-up at line 1704 says to add a second fallback face for each real face, from the device's own serif, with its numbers worked out the same way, after the Georgia one in each stack; that edits src/styles/themes/heritage.css and its tests (heritage-css.test.ts, heritage-edges.test.ts, heritage-scope-edges.test.tsx), which are then listed under Files beyond the step's list with the reason. (7) The layout waits for themeHeritage, and the look waits for newLook. src/lib/features.ts has newLook at line 44 and themeHeritage at line 50, whose comment says it shows only when newLook is on as well (decision at line 932); nothing in src reads FEATURES.themeHeritage today. The manifest gates the layout and the editors' reset on themeHeritage alone; the heritage colours and the heritage.css rules already wait for :root[data-look="new"]. So with themeHeritage on and newLook off the six pages are wrapped but look as today, and with themeHeritage off nothing is wrapped. Gate on themeHeritage alone as the manifest says, and test both cases in the unit runner with FEATURES mocked (test/unit/brand-placements.test.tsx, lines 41 to 57, is the pattern). The browser-test builds cannot show the first case: test/a11y/global-setup.ts (lines 73 and 74) builds dist-a11y-on with VITE_FLAGS=newLook,themeHeritage and dist-a11y-off with none, and test/a11y/builds.spec.ts, test/unit/prepaint-gate.test.ts and test/unit/feature-overrides.test.ts pin those two builds' switches, so leave them. (8) GovernanceDocuments is drawn five times by two pages, and its form is a card, not a form element. BylawsPage draws it three times (lines 20, 21 and 24, layout="preview") and MinutesPage twice (lines 16 and 17), each with isAdmin. In GovernanceDocuments.tsx the editor is lazy (lines 27 to 29) behind LazyEditor with its own Suspense (lines 33 to 45), called at lines 285 and 324, both inside the add or edit card that renders only for an admin who is adding (the block that opens at line 269). Wrap that card, and with it both editor calls, in ThemeScope scope="base" (its default display: contents adds no box) only when FEATURES.themeHeritage is on; with the flag off there is no wrapper and the markup is today's. The component's own layout prop ('accordion' or 'preview') has nothing to do with ThemeScope's layout prop. The list of documents (DocumentCard) stays in heritage: do not wrap it. A base scope with no scope around it is allowed by nestingProblem, so check that no console.warn is raised with the component drawn inside the layout or outside it. test/unit/governanceEditors.test.tsx does not exist. The manifest's risk is that the editor's library needs browser APIs the unit runner's DOM lacks (getClientRects, elementFromPoint): shim them in the test file, never in src. The test renders HeritageLayout with a child route drawing GovernanceDocuments for an admin (mock the module it imports its API from, @/lib/api, and FEATURES), opens Add document, waits for the lazy editor, and asserts that the closest [data-theme] above the editor and above the title field is the base wrapper, whose attribute is "" (an attribute that is present and empty), with the heritage container above that; and that with themeHeritage off the markup holds no ThemeScope wrapper (no [data-theme] at all). (9) AC13 cannot hold with heritage's tokens as pinned today; measure it first. Under newLook in the light look heritage changes these semantic tokens among the base ones: --field, --gold-ink, --ground, --hairline, --ink-muted, --raised, --surface and --surface-2 (src/index.css lines 603 to 615 against the base block at lines 395 to 415; test/unit/tokens-scopes.test.ts lines 33 to 39 pins exactly that list, and test/a11y/scope-switch.spec.ts expects the primary Button's ink and the field border to change between scopes). The shadcn variables are repointed in every scope by the rule at src/index.css lines 693 to 722: --primary-foreground is --ground, --input is --field, --border is --hairline, and --secondary and --muted are --surface-2. So in the light look the default Button's text is #f7f3e8 in heritage and #ffffff in base, the outline Button's ground and border (--ground, --hairline) and the secondary Button's ground (--surface-2) differ, and the Input's ground (bg-background is --ground), border (border-input is --field, #857d6b against #7c8496) and placeholder (--ink-muted) differ; the status badges use status tokens that heritage leaves alone, and the focus ring (--focus) is the same navy in both. In dark mode heritage's grounds were written equal to the base dark ones (lines 620 to 630 against 457 to 472), so dark should match; measure it. Two more things make a plain element screenshot differ whatever the tokens do: a rounded control's corner pixels blend with whatever is behind it (paper against white), and the focus ring is an outline 2px outside the element's box (src/index.css line 730 onward), so an element clip leaves it out. Do this. First take the same-run screenshots and name every control and state that differs and the token that causes it (the record carries the numbers). Then fix the cause in the colour layer, not by styling controls in heritage.css (test/unit/heritage-css.test.ts forbids any control selector there), and without editing the ui components unless nothing else works; one way is to repoint the control-facing shadcn variables inside the heritage block of src/index.css to the base values while the grounds, cards, ink and rules stay as designed, with the layout's own ground taken through bg-ground. Every pin the change moves (tokens-scopes.test.ts, themeScopes.test.ts lines 45 to 70, contrast.test.ts's rows for the looks, scope-switch.spec.ts's expected colours, heritage-scope-edges.test.tsx) is listed under Files beyond the step's list with the reason, and src/index.css grows the production stylesheet only by what that needs (report the bytes). Make the comparison honest: take both samples on the same ground behind the control (for example a padded clip over the same plain box placed behind each sample by the test), include the ring by clipping outside the box, compare the images byte for byte, run light and dark, take the controls from the heritage fixture and the base fixture of the same run, and show the check fails on a planted difference (one control given another colour inside one scope). If a difference remains that cannot be removed without changing the components, do not weaken the test: report the measurement, say what was tried, and stop that part.
